findings.issue: RESOLVED-BY-298f97e. Prior finding: parseHandle cast the parsed `ref` wholesale with no shape validation, so a crafted wire string `{...,ref:{kind:'record',...,data:{ssn}}}` deserialized into a validly-BRANDED ObjectHandle whose `ref` carried a record payload, riding past assertVariableValue (which short-circuits ok:true on isObjectHandle BEFORE structural inspection). Independent re-verification (run rt-choros, 2026-06-10) confirms the FIX closes the ref vector: validateAndReconstructRef() switch-on-kind reconstructs ResourceRef from known identity fields only and throws MalformedHandleError on any payload key (data/fields/payload/view/snapshot), unknown/extra key, kind/field-type mismatch, or unknown kind. Adversarial re-probe of the ref surface (non-forbidden record key, recordId-as-object, __proto__ injection, loose kind with record fields, unknown kind) is REJECTED in every case; no prototype pollution. The exact R-1 repro now throws MalformedHandleError. Honest round-trip (AC-7) preserved for all three ref kinds.
findings.suggestion: Resolved. Keep validateAndReconstructRef as the single ref-deserialization chokepoint.

findings.issue: RESOLVED-BY-4df5c4b. Prior finding: parseHandle cast `facet` wholesale, so a wire facet `{fields:['a'],data:{ssn}}` rode into a branded handle. Independent re-verification (run rt-choros, 2026-06-10) confirms the FIX: parseHandle now routes facet through validateAndReconstructFacet(), which rejects any key other than `fields`, any non-array `fields`, and any non-string element, throwing MalformedHandleError. Adversarial re-probe (facet with data/payload/view keys, object element in fields, non-array fields, facet:null) is rejected/normalized in every case; the honest `{fields:[...]}` facet still round-trips (AC-7). The R-2 facet-payload vector is closed.
findings.suggestion: Resolved. Keep validateAndReconstructFacet as the single facet-deserialization chokepoint.

findings.issue: RESOLVED-BY-4df5c4b. Prior finding: parseHandle did not enforce makeHandle's cross-tenant binding, so a wire ref whose tenantId != envelope tenantId minted a cross-tenant handle. Independent re-verification (run rt-choros, 2026-06-10) confirms the FIX: parseHandle now feeds the validated (ref, tenantId, facet) into makeHandle, which throws CrossTenantHandleError when any tenant-scoped ref component != envelope tenantId. Adversarial re-probe (record/registry/application wire ref with mismatched tenantId) throws CrossTenantHandleError in every case, at parity with makeHandle. The generalization (parseHandle ⊆ makeHandle) holds for the wire-structural surface: every parsed component is forced through makeHandle, so parseHandle returns only handles makeHandle could have produced. R-3 closed.
findings.suggestion: Resolved. Keep parseHandle routing all components through makeHandle so future makeHandle invariants are inherited automatically.

findings.issue: NEW SIBLING — opacity bypass the parse⊆make generalization does NOT touch, because the vector is the IN-MEMORY brand, not the wire. The runtime brand `_RUNTIME_BRAND` is attached via Object.assign as an ENUMERABLE own symbol property. Enumerable own symbols are copied by object spread and Object.assign. Therefore `{ ...genuineHandle }` produces a NON-frozen object that STILL carries the brand and STILL passes isObjectHandle — i.e. the brand IS forgeable outside the module (not by inventing the symbol, but by copying it off any legitimately-held handle). An attacker/connector then attaches a record payload onto the spread-clone and it rides past the runtime opacity edge. Repro (verified live, rt-choros 2026-06-10): const h=makeHandle({kind:'record',tenantId:T,registryId:T,recordId:T},T); const forged={...h}; forged.data={ssn:'123-45-6789'}; isObjectHandle(forged)===true; assertVariableValue(forged)==={ok:true}; forged now has a .data accessor carrying record content. This directly violates the brand's own documented contract (line 64-66 'un-forgeable outside this module'), FR-2/AC-2 ('the handle exposes no field accessor', 'branded/nominal opaque type'), and the runtime opacity invariant (assertVariableValue line 526 trusts the brand and short-circuits ok:true BEFORE any record-shape inspection — identical short-circuit R-1/R-2 exploited). `{...handle, ...}` is an everyday clone idiom in engine/connector/EL code, so this is not merely theoretical: any spread of a handle yields a payload-capable carrier the variable guard blesses. The existing suite is green only because no test asserts brand non-enumerability / spread-clone rejection.
findings.suggestion: Make the brand a NON-ENUMERABLE own property so spread / Object.assign / JSON do not copy it: Object.defineProperty(h, _RUNTIME_BRAND, { value: true, enumerable: false, writable: false, configurable: false }) before freezing (and keep the explicit identity keys enumerable for serializeHandle's field reads, which read named props directly, not via enumeration — round-trip unaffected). Locally-verified: with a non-enumerable brand, `isObjectHandle({...h})===false` and Object.assign({},h) is not a handle, while genuine makeHandle/parseHandle handles still pass. Add an FF-9 test: a spread-clone of a real handle (with a .data attached) must fail isObjectHandle AND assertVariableValue must reject it; genuine handles still pass. Apply in both makeHandle and (inherited via makeHandle) parseHandle.

acceptance_coverage.note: R-4: brand is enumerable, so a spread-clone forges the brand and can carry a .data accessor — violates 'no payload accessor' / 'un-forgeable nominal brand'. Re-true once the brand is non-enumerable.
R-3 resolved: parseHandle now inherits makeHandle's cross-tenant rejection.
